recent_posts.title: Secure your environment variables from AI assistants using 1Password CLI
recent_posts.summary: AI coding assistants can inadvertently read sensitive credentials from .env files, creating security risks. Instead of storing secrets in plain text, use 1Password CLI to store references in .env files (like op://vault/item/field) and inject actual values at runtime with the op run command. This keeps secrets out of AI context windows and version control while maintaining a simple workflow. The setup involves installing 1Password CLI, connecting it to the desktop app, and updating .env files to use vault references instead of raw credentials.

recent_posts.title: Automating issue tracking with Goose and Playwright MCP
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to automating repetitive issue tracking tasks using Goose (an open-source AI agent by Block), Playwright MCP, and the Playwright MCP Bridge Chrome extension. The setup allows an AI agent to interact with web applications through an already-authenticated browser session, eliminating manual login requirements and context switching. The author demonstrates how to configure these tools to automatically create multiple tickets in an issue tracker by simply reading notes aloud, while Playwright MCP handles the browser interactions intelligently without requiring explicit element selectors.

recent_posts.title: Practical tips for writing playwright tests with cursor ai
recent_posts.summary: Practical guide for writing Playwright tests using Cursor AI assistant, covering project rules configuration, custom commands, selector strategies, screenshot usage for context, MCP debugging workflows, and organic rule development. Emphasizes staying with auto model selection, creating custom rules incrementally based on mistakes, using visual context effectively, and leveraging AI for debugging rather than initial test generation. Highlights the critical importance of testing in AI-generated code and encourages personalizing workflows through experimentation.

recent_posts.title: 2FA testing with Playwright and Mailosaur
recent_posts.summary: Demonstrates how to automate two-factor authentication testing using Playwright and Mailosaur. Covers three authentication methods: email magic links, SMS verification codes, and TOTP authenticator apps. Shows how to programmatically access virtual email addresses and phone numbers, extract verification codes, and handle time-sensitive TOTP tokens. Includes practical code examples for each authentication flow, timeout handling, and inbox cleanup strategies.

recent_posts.title: Testing Will Become More Important, Not Less
recent_posts.summary: LLMs are accelerating code generation, but quality concerns persist, making testing more crucial. AI-generated tests will supplement manual testing to enhance efficiency, while human expertise remains essential for designing and reviewing tests. Observability tools will become key in improving AI-generated code reliability.

recent_posts.title: Understanding timeouts in WebdriverIO
recent_posts.summary: Timeouts are crucial for UI end-to-end testing in WebdriverIO as they allow scripts to continue once desired actions occur within the set period. Unlike hard waits, timeouts enable continuous connection to the application, making tests more efficient. The timeout settings can be configured in WebdriverIO and adjusted based on individual command needs. Proper configuration ensures tests run smoothly even with random delays in UI elements' appearances.

recent_posts.title: Test like a developer, develop like a tester
recent_posts.summary: Exploring the dual role of being both a developer and tester, this piece emphasizes the importance of collaboration between the two roles. It discusses the benefits of understanding and bridging the gap between development and testing, and suggests ways testers and developers can work together to enhance software quality. Concepts like test automation, shifting left, and the DRY principle are highlighted as key strategies for better integration and effective testing practices.

recent_posts.title: Laid off as a tester. What now?
recent_posts.summary: The field of QA testing is rapidly changing, and layoffs are becoming more common. Testers should assess their skills and consider alternative roles like product owner or scrum master, which might still leverage their expertise. Learning test automation through resources like Test Automation University and enhancing skills with AI can be beneficial. Making your work visible via GitHub, starting a blog, and networking at meetups can also open new opportunities. It's crucial to stay adaptable and prepared for job market fluctuations.

recent_posts.title: Testing as an entry gate to IT
recent_posts.summary: Testing can be a great entry gate into the world of IT, providing a smoother career transition for individuals with no experience in the field. However, this perspective can be controversial as it may undermine the expertise and value of experienced testers. While testing does not require technical skills, it demands strong human skills and empathy towards software users. Becoming a great tester involves continuous learning and acquiring analytical capabilities. The testing profession has evolved to encompass various specialties, offering opportunities for specialization and the intersection of different professions.
